skill.name: autonomous-ci
skill.description: Guides agents to verify local tests and GitHub CI before reporting work as complete.
skill.summary: Require local test and GitHub CI evidence before completion claims.
skill.author: ANcpLua

security_audit.summary: Several Markdown fence detections are false positives, but the skill intentionally directs agents to run local build and test commands, use GitHub CLI, and collect CI results. The highest risk is the mandatory commit-and-push workflow, which can mutate local and remote repository state without a separate consent gate. No credential exfiltration endpoint or explicit prompt injection to bypass security review was found.

remediation.issue: The workflow requires git add, commit, and push before completion.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before staging, committing, or pushing. Make remote writes optional and document a read-only verification mode.

remediation.issue: The skill uses broad mandatory and no-exceptions language.
remediation.suggestion: State that user and system instructions take precedence. Scope the skill to user-approved CI verification tasks only.

remediation.issue: Local test commands can execute repository-defined scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Tell agents to inspect package scripts or build hooks before running them in untrusted repositories.

remediation.issue: GitHub CLI commands access remote CI data using authenticated state.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose that gh commands contact GitHub and may retrieve repository logs. Ask before downloading or sharing CI logs.

content.value_statement: Agents can report work as done before local tests and CI prove it. This skill defines a verification workflow that checks tests, GitHub Actions, failures, and final evidence.
actual_capabilities: Defines a step-by-step local test and CI verification protocol.
Lists common test commands for .NET, Node.js, Python, and Go projects.
Shows GitHub CLI commands for finding, watching, and inspecting workflow runs.
Describes how to collect failed CI logs and repeat verification after fixes.
Provides a concise success report format with local test counts, CI status, workflow links, and commit data.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI to be installed, authenticated, and authorized for the repository.
Assumes GitHub Actions; other CI systems need manual adaptation.
Can suggest commits and pushes, so users should require explicit approval for remote writes.
Cannot prove correctness beyond the project tests and workflows that already exist.

use_cases.title: Verify a code fix before handoff
use_cases.description: Run local tests, monitor GitHub Actions, and report completion only after evidence is available.

use_cases.title: Gate pull request readiness
use_cases.description: Check that build, test, and lint workflows pass before asking for review or merging work.

use_cases.title: Investigate CI failures
use_cases.description: Download failed workflow logs, identify likely causes, apply fixes, and repeat the verification loop.

prompt_templates.title: Verify my change
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner verification for one completed change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the autonomous CI workflow for my latest change. Run local verification, then summarize what passed and what still needs attention.

prompt_templates.title: Check GitHub Actions
prompt_templates.scenario: Standard local and remote CI check.
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify this branch with local tests and GitHub Actions. Ask before any commit or push, and include workflow links in the result.

prompt_templates.title: Debug failed CI
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate investigation after a workflow failure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the CI failure protocol. Inspect failed workflow logs, explain the likely root cause, fix it, and rerun local verification before reporting status.

prompt_templates.title: Apply a release gate
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced verification before a release or merge.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the full verification gate for this release branch. Confirm local tests, all required workflows, failure evidence, and final completion evidence.

output_examples.input: Verify the latest bug fix before I open a pull request.
output_examples.output: Local tests passed. GitHub Actions completed successfully for build, test, and lint. The response includes workflow links and the verified commit.

output_examples.input: CI failed after my push. Find out why.
output_examples.output: The failed workflow log points to a test assertion in the payment module. The report names the failing check and recommends the next fix.

output_examples.input: Can we call this task complete?
output_examples.output: Not yet. Local tests passed, but one remote workflow is still running. Completion should wait for the final CI result.

best_practices: Ask for explicit permission before staging, committing, or pushing changes.
Run the smallest useful local verification first, then confirm all required remote workflows.
Include concrete evidence such as test counts, workflow names, conclusions, links, and commit identifiers.
anti_patterns: Do not claim success based only on confidence or local reasoning.
Do not ignore a failed or still-running CI workflow.
Do not push code automatically when the user only asked for analysis or review.

faq.question: Does this skill run CI by itself?
faq.answer: It provides instructions for an agent to run local commands and monitor GitHub Actions. Tool execution still depends on the host agent.

faq.question: Which CI service does it support?
faq.answer: The examples focus on GitHub Actions through the GitHub CLI. Other CI systems require manual changes to the workflow.

faq.question: Can it be used without pushing code?
faq.answer: Yes, use it for local verification and read-only CI checks. Remote writes should require explicit user approval.

faq.question: What project types are covered?
faq.answer: The examples cover .NET, Node.js, Python, and Go test commands. Other stacks need project-specific commands.

faq.question: What evidence should the final response include?
faq.answer: A good report includes local test status, workflow names, CI conclusions, links or logs, commit identity, and remaining risks.

faq.question: Is this safe for untrusted repositories?
faq.answer: Use caution. Test scripts and build hooks can execute code from the repository, so review commands before running them.
